# Technical Documentation — LGIPDB01

**Program:** `lgipdb01.cbl`  
**Type:** CICS DB2 Data Management — Inquire Policy  
**Audience:** Developer  
**Generated:** 2025  

---

## Overview

`LGIPDB01` is the **DB2 data management layer** for inquiring (reading) insurance policies. Called via `EXEC CICS LINK` from `LGIPOL01`, it routes by `CA-REQUEST-ID` to execute the appropriate DB2 SELECT and populate the COMMAREA with policy details.

Supports **7 inquiry variants** for different policy types and retrieval modes:

| Request ID | Operation | DB2 Approach |
|---|---|---|
| `01IEND` | Inquire Endowment by policy number | Single SELECT on POLICY + ENDOWMENT |
| `01IHOU` | Inquire House by policy number | Single SELECT on POLICY + HOUSE |
| `01IMOT` | Inquire Motor by policy number | Single SELECT on POLICY + MOTOR |
| `01ICOM` | Inquire Commercial by customer + policy | Single SELECT on POLICY + COMMERCIAL |
| `02ICOM` | Inquire Commercial by policy number only | Single SELECT on POLICY + COMMERCIAL |
| `03ICOM` | Inquire all Commercial for a customer | Cursor `Cust_Cursor` — up to 20 rows |
| `05ICOM` | Inquire Commercial by ZIP/postcode | Cursor `Zip_Cursor` — all matching rows |

---

## Inputs

| Source | Field | Description |
|---|---|---|
| COMMAREA | `CA-REQUEST-ID` | Determines which SELECT variant to execute |
| COMMAREA | `CA-CUSTOMER-NUM` | Customer number (used as DB2 host variable) |
| COMMAREA | `CA-POLICY-NUM` | Policy number to retrieve |
| COMMAREA | `CA-B-POSTCODE` | Used only for `05ICOM` ZIP code cursor |

---

## DB2 Cursors Declared

| Cursor | Used By | Filter |
|---|---|---|
| `Cust_Cursor` | `03ICOM` | Joins POLICY + COMMERCIAL WHERE CustomerNumber = :DB2-CUSTOMERNUM-INT |
| `Zip_Cursor` | `05ICOM` | Joins POLICY + COMMERCIAL WHERE Commercial.Zipcode = :CA-B-POSTCODE |

---

## Programs Called

| Program | Call Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `LGSTSQ` | `EXEC CICS LINK` | Error message writer |

---

## Copybooks / SQL Includes

| Include | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `LGPOLICY` (SQL INCLUDE) | DB2 record structures and length constants |
| `LGCMAREA` (SQL INCLUDE) | COMMAREA structure |
| `SQLCA` | DB2 SQLCODE / SQLSTATE |

---

## Error Handling

| SQLCODE | Return Code | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `'00'` | Row found — data moved to COMMAREA |
| 100 | `'01'` | No rows found — invalid customer/policy combination |
| Other | `'90'` | DB2 error — logged to LGSTSQ |
| Cursor open failure | `'89'` | Cursor error — logged to LGSTSQ |
| Cursor close failure | `'88'` | Cursor error — logged to LGSTSQ |

---

## Business Rules

1. **NULL handling**: `BROKERID`, `BROKERSREFERENCE`, `PAYMENT` use indicator variables — NULL values are not moved to COMMAREA
2. **Endowment VARCHAR**: `PADDINGDATA` length is checked via indicator variable; data moved conditionally
3. **`FINAL` marker**: Written to first 5 bytes of the trailing FILLER field after policy data — signals end-of-data to caller
4. **Commercial cursor limit**: `03ICOM` cursor capped at 20 records — `ICOM-Record-Count > 20` forces SQLCODE=17 to exit loop
5. **COMMAREA size check**: If retrieved data would exceed received COMMAREA size → RC `'98'`, RETURN

# Technical Documentation — LGAPVS01

**Program:** `lgapvs01.cbl`  
**Type:** CICS VSAM Data Management — Add Policy  
**Audience:** Developer  
**Generated:** 2025  

---

## Overview

`LGAPVS01` is the **VSAM data management layer** for writing a new policy to the `KSDSPOLY` VSAM KSDS file. Called via `EXEC CICS LINK` from `LGAPDB01` (after a successful DB2 INSERT), it writes a fixed-length 64-byte summary record to the VSAM secondary store.

This is the **second phase** of the two-phase commit pattern: DB2 (primary) → VSAM (secondary, on DB2 success only).

---

## VSAM Record Structure (`WF-Policy-Info`)

| Field | Size | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `WF-Request-ID` | 1 byte | Policy type character: `C`, `E`, `H`, or `M` |
| `WF-Customer-Num` | 10 bytes | Customer number (from `CA-CUSTOMER-NUM`) |
| `WF-Policy-Num` | 10 bytes | Policy number (from `CA-POLICY-NUM`) |
| `WF-Policy-Data` | 43 bytes | Type-specific summary data (see below) |
| **Total** | **64 bytes** | Fixed record length |

### Policy-Specific Data (`WF-Policy-Data` REDEFINES)

| Type | Fields Stored |
|---|---|
| **C** (Commercial) | `WF-B-Postcode` (8), `WF-B-Status` (4), `WF-B-Customer` (31) |
| **E** (Endowment) | `WF-E-WITH-PROFITS` (1), `WF-E-EQUITIES` (1), `WF-E-MANAGED-FUND` (1), `WF-E-FUND-NAME` (10), `WF-E-LIFE-ASSURED` (30) |
| **H** (House) | `WF-H-PROPERTY-TYPE` (15), `WF-H-BEDROOMS` (3), `WF-H-VALUE` (8), `WF-H-POSTCODE` (8), `WF-H-HOUSE-NAME` (9) |
| **M** (Motor) | `WF-M-MAKE` (15), `WF-M-MODEL` (15), `WF-M-VALUE` (6), `WF-M-REGNUMBER` (7) |

---

## VSAM Key (`WF-Policy-Key` — 21 bytes)

| Component | Size | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `WF-Request-ID` | 1 | 4th char of `CA-REQUEST-ID` (e.g., `01AMOT` → `M`) |
| `WF-Customer-Num` | 10 | `CA-CUSTOMER-NUM` |
| `WF-Policy-Num` | 10 | `CA-POLICY-NUM` |

---

## Processing Logic

1. Extract `WF-Request-ID` from `CA-REQUEST-ID(4:1)` — the policy type character
2. Copy `CA-POLICY-NUM` and `CA-CUSTOMER-NUM` to key fields
3. **EVALUATE `WF-Request-ID`** — populate type-specific `WF-Policy-Data` from COMMAREA
4. **EXEC CICS WRITE FILE('KSDSPOLY')** — write 64-byte record with 21-byte key
5. If `WS-RESP ≠ DFHRESP(NORMAL)` → `CA-RETURN-CODE = '80'`, log error, RETURN

---

## Programs Called

| Program | Call Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `LGSTSQ` | `EXEC CICS LINK` | Error message writer (on VSAM write failure only) |

---

## Error Handling

| Condition | Return Code |
|---|---|
| `CICS WRITE` `RESP ≠ NORMAL` | `'80'` — logs RESP, RESP2, customer/policy numbers to LGSTSQ |

---

## Business Rules

1. VSAM stores only a **summary** of the policy — not the full DB2 record
2. Called **only after** successful DB2 INSERT in LGAPDB01 (two-phase pattern)
3. The VSAM key includes the **policy type** as first byte — allows type-aware lookups
4. `WHEN OTHER` in the EVALUATE moves SPACES to `WF-Policy-Data` — prevents garbage data

# Technical Documentation — LGSTSQ

**Program:** `lgstsq.cbl`  
**Type:** CICS Utility — Error/Message Writer  
**Audience:** Developer  
**Generated:** 2025  

---

## Overview

`LGSTSQ` is GenApp's **centralized error logging utility**. It writes diagnostic messages to two destinations simultaneously:
1. **CSMT TDQ** (Transient Data Queue) — CICS system message log
2. **GENAERRS TSQ** (Temporary Storage Queue) — GenApp-specific error store (browsable)

It can be invoked in two modes:
- **CICS LINK** (from another program) — writes the COMMAREA content as the message
- **Terminal transaction** — receives data from the terminal and writes it

---

## Inputs

| Mode | Input | Description |
|---|---|---|
| LINK mode | `DFHCOMMAREA` (`COMMA-DATA`, 90 bytes) | Message text passed from calling program |
| Transaction mode | Terminal 3270 input | First 5 bytes = transaction ID, next 74 bytes = message |

---

## Queue Names

| Queue | Type | Default Name | Override |
|---|---|---|---|
| System log | TDQ | `CSMT` | Fixed |
| GenApp store | TSQ | `GENAERRS` | Pass `Q=xxxx` prefix in message to use `GENAxxxx` |

---

## Processing Logic

1. **Determine invocation mode**:
   - `ASSIGN INVOKINGPROG` — if non-blank → LINK mode (`WS-FLAG = 'C'`)
   - Otherwise → transaction mode (`EXEC CICS RECEIVE`) (`WS-FLAG = 'R'`)
2. **Build write message**: prefix with SYSID (4 bytes) + space + message (90 bytes)
3. **Check for queue override**: if message starts with `Q=`, extract 4-char suffix → TSQ name = `GENAxxxx`
4. **WRITEQ TD QUEUE('CSMT')** — write to system TDQ
5. **WRITEQ TS QUEUE(STSQ-NAME)** — write to GenApp TSQ (NOSUSPEND — drops if no storage)
6. **If transaction mode**: send blank screen to terminal (`EXEC CICS SEND TEXT ... FREEKB`)
7. **CICS RETURN**

---

## Callers (Programs that LINK to LGSTSQ)

Every GenApp program calls `LGSTSQ` in its `WRITE-ERROR-MESSAGE` procedure:

| Program | When Called |
|---|---|
| `LGAPOL01`, `LGIPOL01`, `LGUPOL01`, `LGDPOL01` | COMMAREA errors (missing/short) |
| `LGAPDB01`, `LGIPDB01`, `LGUPDB01`, `LGDPDB01` | DB2 SQL errors (non-zero SQLCODE) |
| `LGAPVS01`, `LGIPVS01`, `LGUPVS01`, `LGDPVS01` | VSAM CICS WRITE/READ failures |

---

## Business Rules

1. **NOSUSPEND** on TSQ write — if TS storage is exhausted, the write is silently dropped (no error)
2. **Two writes** per call — TDQ for operations teams (CSMT), TSQ for developers (GENAERRS)
3. **Queue override** (`Q=xxxx`) allows routing error messages to a specific sub-queue for targeted debugging
4. This program is invoked by **all** GenApp programs for error logging — it is the single point of error persistence

# Technical Documentation — LGDPDB01

**Program:** `lgdpdb01.cbl`  
**Type:** CICS DB2 Data Management — Delete Policy  
**Audience:** Developer  
**Generated:** 2025  

---

## Overview

`LGDPDB01` is the **DB2 data management layer** for deleting an insurance policy. Called via `EXEC CICS LINK` from `LGDPOL01`, it performs DB2 DELETE operations to remove the policy from the `POLICY` table and the type-specific table.

DB2 referential integrity with CASCADE DELETE handles removal from the type-specific table automatically when the POLICY row is deleted (if foreign keys are set up with CASCADE). Otherwise, a two-step delete is performed.

---

## Inputs

| Source | Field | Description |
|---|---|---|
| COMMAREA | `CA-REQUEST-ID` | `01DEND`, `01DHOU`, `01DMOT`, `01DCOM` |
| COMMAREA | `CA-CUSTOMER-NUM` | Customer number — used to scope the delete |
| COMMAREA | `CA-POLICY-NUM` | Policy number to delete |

---

## Processing Logic

1. **Initialize working storage**
2. **COMMAREA validation** — EIBCALEN check
3. **EVALUATE `CA-REQUEST-ID`** — routes to type-specific DELETE paragraph
4. **DELETE from `POLICY` table** WHERE `POLICYNUMBER = :DB2-POLICYNUM-INT` AND `CUSTOMERNUMBER = :DB2-CUSTOMERNUM-INT`
5. **Check SQLCODE** — handle not-found (100) and error cases
6. **CICS RETURN**

---

## Programs Called

| Program | Call Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `LGSTSQ` | `EXEC CICS LINK` | Error message writer |

---

## Copybooks / SQL Includes

| Include | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `LGCMAREA` | COMMAREA structure |
| `LGPOLICY` | DB2 record structures |
| `SQLCA` | DB2 SQLCODE |

---

## Error Handling

| SQLCODE | Return Code | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `'00'` | Delete successful |
| 100 | `'01'` | Row not found — policy/customer combination invalid |
| Other | `'90'` | DB2 error |

---

## Business Rules

1. Delete is scoped to **both** customer number AND policy number — prevents accidental cross-customer deletes
2. All four policy types (E, H, M, C) are supported
3. VSAM delete is handled separately (by `LGDPVS01` if called)

# Technical Documentation — LGUPDB01

**Program:** `lgupdb01.cbl`  
**Type:** CICS DB2 Data Management — Update Policy  
**Audience:** Developer  
**Generated:** 2025  

---

## Overview

`LGUPDB01` is the **DB2 data management layer** for updating an insurance policy. Called via `EXEC CICS LINK` from `LGUPOL01`, it performs DB2 UPDATE operations on the POLICY table and the type-specific table for the policy being modified.

---

## Inputs

| Source | Field | Description |
|---|---|---|
| COMMAREA | `CA-REQUEST-ID` | `01UEND`, `01UHOU`, `01UMOT` |
| COMMAREA | `CA-POLICY-NUM` | Policy number to update |
| COMMAREA | `CA-CUSTOMER-NUM` | Customer number |
| COMMAREA | `CA-POLICY-COMMON` | Updated common fields |
| COMMAREA | Policy-specific fields | Updated type-specific fields |

---

## DB2 Operations

### POLICY table UPDATE
Updates `EXPIRYDATE`, `LASTCHANGED (CURRENT TIMESTAMP)`, `BROKERID`, `BROKERSREFERENCE`, `PAYMENT` WHERE `POLICYNUMBER = :DB2-POLICYNUM-INT`.

### ENDOWMENT UPDATE (`01UEND`)
Updates `WITHPROFITS`, `EQUITIES`, `MANAGEDFUND`, `FUNDNAME`, `TERM`, `SUMASSURED`, `LIFEASSURED` WHERE `POLICYNUMBER = :DB2-POLICYNUM-INT`.

### HOUSE UPDATE (`01UHOU`)
Updates `PROPERTYTYPE`, `BEDROOMS`, `VALUE`, `HOUSENAME`, `HOUSENUMBER`, `POSTCODE` WHERE `POLICYNUMBER = :DB2-POLICYNUM-INT`.

### MOTOR UPDATE (`01UMOT`)
Updates `MAKE`, `MODEL`, `VALUE`, `REGNUMBER`, `COLOUR`, `CC`, `YEAROFMANUFACTURE`, `PREMIUM`, `ACCIDENTS` WHERE `POLICYNUMBER = :DB2-POLICYNUM-INT`.

---

## Programs Called

| Program | Call Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `LGSTSQ` | `EXEC CICS LINK` | Error message writer |

---

## Copybooks / SQL Includes

| Include | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `LGCMAREA` | COMMAREA structure |
| `LGPOLICY` | DB2 record structures and length constants |
| `SQLCA` | DB2 SQLCODE |

---

## Error Handling

| SQLCODE | Return Code |
|---|---|
| 0 | `'00'` — success |
| 100 | `'01'` — not found |
| Other | `'90'` — DB2 error |

---

## Business Rules

1. `LASTCHANGED` is set to `CURRENT TIMESTAMP` on every update — audit trail
2. Commercial update (`01UCOM`) is **not supported** in this program — falls through with RC `'99'` from `LGUPOL01`
3. Two-step update: POLICY header first, then type-specific table

# Technical Documentation — LGDPVS01 / LGIPVS01 / LGUPVS01 / LGDPDB01 / LGASTAT1

**Programs:** `lgdpvs01.cbl`, `lgipvs01.cbl`, `lgupvs01.cbl`, `lgastat1.cbl`  
**Type:** CICS VSAM Data Management + Statistics  
**Audience:** Developer  
**Generated:** 2025  

---

## LGDPVS01 — Delete Policy VSAM

### Overview
Deletes a policy record from the `KSDSPOLY` VSAM KSDS file. Called from `LGDPDB01` after the DB2 DELETE.

### Processing
1. Extract policy type from `CA-REQUEST-ID(4:1)`, construct 21-byte key
2. `EXEC CICS DELETE FILE('KSDSPOLY') RIDFLD(WF-Policy-Key) KEYLENGTH(21)`
3. If `RESP ≠ NORMAL` and `RESP ≠ NOTFND` → RC `'80'`, log to LGSTSQ

### Business Rules
- NOTFOUND on DELETE is **not** treated as an error — VSAM is a secondary store; DB2 is authoritative
- Key structure: policy type (1) + customer number (10) + policy number (10)

---

## LGIPVS01 — Inquire Policy VSAM

### Overview
Reads a policy summary record from `KSDSPOLY` VSAM KSDS. Used as an alternative data retrieval path or for summary data.

### Processing
1. Construct 21-byte key from request ID, customer number, policy number
2. `EXEC CICS READ FILE('KSDSPOLY') INTO(WF-Policy-Info) RIDFLD(WF-Policy-Key) KEYLENGTH(21)`
3. Move type-specific VSAM fields back to appropriate COMMAREA fields
4. If `RESP ≠ NORMAL` → RC `'80'`, log to LGSTSQ

### Key Points
- Returns **summary data only** — not the full DB2 record
- For complete policy details, use `LGIPDB01` (DB2 path)

---

## LGUPVS01 — Update Policy VSAM

### Overview
Updates a policy summary record in `KSDSPOLY`. Called from `LGUPDB01` after the DB2 UPDATE.

### Processing
1. Construct 21-byte key
2. Read existing record (EXEC CICS READ UPDATE)
3. Overwrite type-specific fields with updated COMMAREA data
4. EXEC CICS REWRITE FILE('KSDSPOLY')
5. If `RESP ≠ NORMAL` → RC `'80'`, log to LGSTSQ

---

## LGASTAT1 — Customer Statistics Collector

### Overview
`LGASTAT1` is a statistics accumulation program that aggregates policy counts per customer. It is called from customer-facing transactions to update running totals.

### Processing
1. Reads customer record from `LGACDB01` (DB2 customer data)  
2. Counts policies per type across the policy layer
3. Calls `LGACVS01` to update the customer VSAM record with the latest counts
4. Returns updated `CA-NUM-POLICIES` in COMMAREA

### Programs Called
| Program | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `LGACDB01` | Read customer details from DB2 |
| `LGACVS01` | Update customer VSAM record with policy counts |
| `LGSTSQ` | Error logging |

### Business Rules
- Statistics are **non-critical** — errors in statistics collection do not ABEND the main transaction
- Policy counts are maintained at the **customer level**, not per policy type

# LAB 2 — Exercise 4: GenApp End-to-End Flow WITH Documentation

**Mode:** Ask  
**Application:** `cics-genapp/base/src/`  
**Documentation:** `docs/` (14 program docs) + `docs/html/` (16 HTML pages)  
**Date:** 2025

---

## Prompt Asked
> "Help me understand the cics-genapp application."

---

## Bob's Answer (With Documentation)

The Add Policy flow in GenApp follows a strict **3-tier pattern**:

---

### Tier 1 — Presentation (3270 BMS)

The user initiates from a transaction code corresponding to their policy type:
- `SSP1` → Motor policy
- `SSP2` → Endowment policy  
- `SSP3` → House policy
- `SSP4` → Commercial policy

The BMS map (`ssmap.bms`) collects policy type-specific input fields and packages them into `DFHCOMMAREA` using the `CA-POLICY-REQUEST` redefine in `lgcmarea.cpy`. The `CA-REQUEST-ID` field (6 chars) encodes both the operation (`A`=Add, `I`=Inquire, `U`=Update, `D`=Delete) and the policy type.

---

### Tier 2 — Business Logic: `lgapol01.cbl`

`LGAPOL01` receives the COMMAREA and:
1. Validates `EIBCALEN ≠ 0` — missing COMMAREA causes `ABEND 'LGCA'` (non-recoverable)
2. Initializes `CA-RETURN-CODE = '00'`
3. Validates minimum COMMAREA length ≥ 28 bytes (`WS-CA-HEADER-LEN`) — short COMMAREA → RC `'98'`
4. Issues `EXEC CICS LINK Program(LGAPDB01) Commarea(DFHCOMMAREA) LENGTH(32500)`
5. Returns to caller via `EXEC CICS RETURN`

**LGAPOL01 is deliberately field-agnostic** — it has no knowledge of individual policy fields. It simply validates the contract and delegates. This is why field-level changes (new columns) never touch this tier.

---

### Tier 3 — Data Management: `lgapdb01.cbl` + `lgapvs01.cbl`

**`LGAPDB01`** performs:

1. **Routes by `CA-REQUEST-ID`** to determine policy type and set `DB2-POLICYTYPE`:
   - `01AEND` → `'E'`, adds `WS-FULL-ENDOW-LEN` (124) to required length
   - `01AHOU` → `'H'`, adds `WS-FULL-HOUSE-LEN` (130)
   - `01AMOT` → `'M'`, adds `WS-FULL-MOTOR-LEN` (137)
   - `01ACOM` → `'C'`, adds `WS-FULL-COMM-LEN` (1174)
2. **`INSERT INTO POLICY`** — `POLICYNUMBER` assigned by DB2 IDENTITY, `LASTCHANGED` set to `CURRENT TIMESTAMP`
3. **Retrieves assigned policy number** via `IDENTITY_VAL_LOCAL()` → `CA-POLICY-NUM` (returned to caller)
4. **`INSERT INTO` type-specific table** (ENDOWMENT/HOUSE/MOTOR/COMMERCIAL)
   - On failure: `ABEND 'LGSQ'` → forces CICS to **backout the POLICY INSERT** (unit of work)
5. **`EXEC CICS LINK Program(LGAPVS01)`** — write VSAM secondary record

**This implements the two-phase commit pattern**: DB2 first, VSAM only on DB2 success.

**`LGAPVS01`** writes a **64-byte summary record** to `KSDSPOLY` VSAM KSDS with key: `[policy type 1 byte] + [customer num 10 bytes] + [policy num 10 bytes]`.

---

### Error Path (Any Tier)

Any error in any program calls `LGSTSQ`, which writes a diagnostic message to:
- **`CSMT` TDQ** — CICS system operations log
- **`GENAERRS` TSQ** — GenApp developer error store (browsable)

---

## 📊 Side-by-Side Comparison: Before vs. After Documentation

| Question | Without Docs (Lab 2 Ex 1) | With Docs (Now) |
|---|---|---|
| Which programs are involved? | "Probably lgapol01, lgapdb01, lgapvs01" (guessed) | Full 3-tier chain confirmed with exact CICS LINK calls |
| What data flows between them? | "COMMAREA, likely lgcmarea.cpy" | Specific: CA-REQUEST-ID routing, CA-RETURN-CODE handshake, WS-FULL-*-LEN from lgpolicy.cpy |
| Where does validation happen? | "Probably in the business logic layer" | Two exact points: EIBCALEN=0 → ABEND LGCA; EIBCALEN < required → RC 98 |
| DB2 write order? | Not answered | POLICY first, then type-specific — ABEND LGSQ if type table fails |
| Policy number assignment? | Not mentioned | DB2 IDENTITY_VAL_LOCAL() → CA-POLICY-NUM returned to caller |
| VSAM write? | "lgapvs01 for secondary store" | Called from LGAPDB01 after DB2 success; writes 64-byte summary; key = type+custnum+polnum |
| Error handling? | Not mentioned | LGSTSQ → GENAERRS TSQ + CSMT TDQ from any tier |
| Confidence | Low — must read 6+ programs | High — grounded in generated documentation |

---

## 🎓 What the Documentation Enabled

1. **Cross-program reasoning** — Bob can trace the full flow across 3 tiers without reading each program
2. **Business-level answers** — "two-phase commit pattern", "unit of work rollback via ABEND LGSQ" are now answerable
3. **Precise field references** — `CA-RETURN-CODE`, `WS-CA-HEADER-LEN`, `IDENTITY_VAL_LOCAL()` — named correctly
4. **Architecture insight** — the "business logic is field-agnostic" principle only becomes visible with cross-program documentation

**The documentation value chain in action:**
```
Source code → Program docs (14 files) → Application HTML (16 pages) → Precise answers
```

# create_html_artifact — one-pager output

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply. Three rules make this concrete:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool
- The tool call must be the last action you take in the turn — do not add more content after it. Keep the surrounding chat message itself to one or two sentences; the artifact should speak for itself.
- Produce a single, self-contained, fully static HTML+CSS document with everything inlined. Content is automatically sanitized on save, and forbidden patterns will be stripped regardless of what you intended, so do not rely on any interactive or unsafe pattern surviving.
- End the document with a small, muted "Made with IBM Bob" footer placed just before `</body>`, centred, roughly 12px, with a thin top border to visually separate it from the content above.
- If you are updating or improving an artifact that already exists, re-use its same `id` so that your new version replaces the old one rather than creating a duplicate.

## Never allowed — always stripped, even if instructed
<script>, inline event handlers (onclick/onload/…), <iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>/<object>/<embed>/<applet>/<portal>, <form>, <link>, <base>, <meta http-equiv>, javascript:/vbscript: URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//…), external URLs in src/poster/… attributes, @import in <style> blocks, url() in <style> blocks unless it is a data: URI.
<a href> to external sites is fine. Inline data: image URIs are fine.

## Design
Single column, max-width ~760px, centred. No animations, gradients, shadows, emojis, or decorative icons. SVG only for data visualisation.
Font: `-apple-system, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`, ~14–15px, line-height ~1.6.
Palette: bg `#ffffff`, surface `#f7f8fa`, border `#e5e7eb`, text `#1f2328`, muted `#57606a`, accent `#3b82d4` (sparingly), secondary `#7c5cd8` (rarely).

# create_chart — chart output
Use the `create_chart` tool when the user asks for a chart or data visualisation.

Call the tool with:
- `type`: one of LineChart | BarChart | PieChart | ScatterChart | RadarChart | BoxplotChart

Generate 6 individual program HTML pages for a GenApp knowledge base, and save them to the following paths under DeveloperDay/docs/html/:

1. lgapol01.html — LGAPOL01 Add Policy Business Logic
2. lgipol01.html — LGIPOL01 Inquire Policy Business Logic  
3. lgupol01.html — LGUPOL01 Update Policy Business Logic
4. lgdpol01.html — LGDPOL01 Delete Policy Business Logic
5. lgapdb01.html — LGAPDB01 Add Policy DB2
6. lgstsq.html — LGSTSQ Error Writer Utility

Each page must be a complete self-contained HTML file with the same nav bar (Home, Architecture, Add Policy, Inquire Policy, Update Policy, Delete Policy, Copybooks), same blue header style (background: #1b3a6b), same nav (background: #254d8c), and same footer "Generated by IBM Bob Premium Package for Z".

Each page must contain:
- Program name and type in header
- Overview paragraph
- Inputs table (Source, Field, Description)
- Processing Logic (numbered steps)
- Programs Called table (Program, Call Type, Purpose) — with clickable links to other program pages
- Copybooks Used table
- Error Handling table
- Business Rules section
- A "Back to Index" link

Use the following content for each program:

**lgapol01.html**: Add Policy BL. Overview: validates COMMAREA, links to LGAPDB01. Inputs: CA-REQUEST-ID (01AEND/01AHOU/01AMOT/01ACOM), CA-CUSTOMER-NUM, CA-POLICY-COMMON, policy-specific fields, EIBCALEN. Logic: initialize, check EIBCALEN=0 → ABEND LGCA, set RC=00, check len < 28 → RC 98, CICS LINK to LGAPDB01 (32500), CICS RETURN. Calls: LGAPDB01 (CICS LINK, DB2 insert), LGSTSQ (error). Copybooks: lgcmarea.cpy, lgpolicy.cpy. Errors: EIBCALEN=0 → ABEND LGCA; len<28 → RC 98. Rules: 1) min 28 bytes 2) field-agnostic 3) policy number assigned by DB2 4) two-phase commit in LGAPDB01.

**lgipol01.html**: Inquire Policy BL. Overview: validates COMMAREA, links to LGIPDB01. Inputs: CA-REQUEST-ID (01IEND/01IHOU/01IMOT/01ICOM/02ICOM/03ICOM/05ICOM), CA-CUSTOMER-NUM, CA-POLICY-NUM, EIBCALEN. Logic: initialize, check EIBCALEN=0 → ABEND LGCA, set RC=00, save EIBCALEN, CICS LINK to LGIPDB01 (32500), CICS RETURN. Calls: LGIPDB01 (CICS LINK, DB2 select), LGSTSQ (error). Copybooks: lgcmarea.cpy, lgpolicy.cpy. Errors: EIBCALEN=0 → ABEND LGCA; all data errors handled in LGIPDB01. Rules: 1) no COMMAREA = ABEND 2) routing by CA-REQUEST-ID happens in LGIPDB01 3) 7 inquiry variants supported.

**lgupol01.html**: Update Policy BL. Inputs: CA-REQUEST-ID (01UEND/01UHOU/01UMOT), EIBCALEN. Logic: EVALUATE CA-REQUEST-ID, check length per type (endow:152, house:158, motor:165), PERFORM UPDATE-POLICY-DB2-INFO → LGUPDB01. Known gap: Commercial update (01UCOM) not supported → RC 99. Calls: LGUPDB01 (CICS LINK), LGSTSQ. Copybooks: lgcmarea.cpy.

**lgdpol01.html**: Delete Policy BL. Inputs: CA-REQUEST-ID (01DEND/01DMOT/01DHOU/01DCOM), EIBCALEN. Logic: upper-case CA-REQUEST-ID, check 4 valid codes, PERFORM DELETE-POLICY-DB2-INFO → LGDPDB01. Calls: LGDPDB01 (CICS LINK), LGSTSQ. Copybooks: lgcmarea.cpy. Rules: all 4 types supported, delete needs header only (28 bytes), CA-REQUEST-ID is upper-cased.

**lgapdb01.html**: Add Policy DB2. Overview: routes by CA-REQUEST-ID, INSERTs to POLICY table then type-specific table (ENDOWMENT/HOUSE/MOTOR/COMMERCIAL), links to LGAPVS01, returns DB2-assigned CA-POLICY-NUM. COMMAREA lengths: Endow +124, House +130, Motor +137, Commercial +1174. DB2: INSERT POLICY (IDENTITY for POLICYNUMBER, CURRENT TIMESTAMP for LASTCHANGED), then type INSERT, then LGAPVS01. ABEND LGSQ on type INSERT failure to backout POLICY INSERT. Calls: LGAPVS01 (CICS LINK, VSAM write), LGSTSQ (error). SQL includes: LGPOLICY, LGCMAREA, SQLCA. Error codes: SQLCODE 0=00, -530=70 (FK), other=90. Rules: ABEND LGSQ ensures unit of work rollback; policy number assigned by IDENTITY; commercial has largest COMMAREA.

**lgstsq.html**: Error Writer Utility. Overview: writes diagnostic messages to CSMT TDQ and GENAERRS TSQ. Two modes: LINK (from program) or transaction (from terminal). Queue override: message starting Q=xxxx routes to GENAxxxx TSQ. NOSUSPEND on TSQ write. Called by ALL GenApp programs. Logic: ASSIGN INVOKINGPROG → if non-blank=LINK mode, else RECEIVE from terminal; build message with SYSID prefix; check Q= prefix; WRITEQ TD CSMT; WRITEQ TS GENAERRS (NOSUSPEND); if terminal mode → SEND TEXT FREEKB; CICS RETURN.

All HTML pages should use consistent styling matching the index/architecture pages (background #f4f6f9, header #1b3a6b, nav #254d8c).

# LAB 2 — Exercise 4: GenApp End-to-End Flow WITH Documentation

**Mode:** Ask  
**Application:** `cics-genapp/base/src/`  
**Documentation:** `docs/` (14 program docs) + `docs/html/` (16 HTML pages)  
**Date:** 2025

---

## Prompt Asked
> "Help me understand the cics-genapp application."

---

## Bob's Answer (With Documentation)

The Add Policy flow in GenApp follows a strict **3-tier pattern**:

---

### Tier 1 — Presentation (3270 BMS)

The user initiates from a transaction code corresponding to their policy type:
- `SSP1` → Motor policy
- `SSP2` → Endowment policy  
- `SSP3` → House policy
- `SSP4` → Commercial policy

The BMS map (`ssmap.bms`) collects policy type-specific input fields and packages them into `DFHCOMMAREA` using the `CA-POLICY-REQUEST` redefine in `lgcmarea.cpy`. The `CA-REQUEST-ID` field (6 chars) encodes both the operation (`A`=Add, `I`=Inquire, `U`=Update, `D`=Delete) and the policy type.

---

### Tier 2 — Business Logic: `lgapol01.cbl`

`LGAPOL01` receives the COMMAREA and:
1. Validates `EIBCALEN ≠ 0` — missing COMMAREA causes `ABEND 'LGCA'` (non-recoverable)
2. Initializes `CA-RETURN-CODE = '00'`
3. Validates minimum COMMAREA length ≥ 28 bytes (`WS-CA-HEADER-LEN`) — short COMMAREA → RC `'98'`
4. Issues `EXEC CICS LINK Program(LGAPDB01) Commarea(DFHCOMMAREA) LENGTH(32500)`
5. Returns to caller via `EXEC CICS RETURN`

**LGAPOL01 is deliberately field-agnostic** — it has no knowledge of individual policy fields. It simply validates the contract and delegates. This is why field-level changes (new columns) never touch this tier.

---

### Tier 3 — Data Management: `lgapdb01.cbl` + `lgapvs01.cbl`

**`LGAPDB01`** performs:

1. **Routes by `CA-REQUEST-ID`** to determine policy type and set `DB2-POLICYTYPE`:
   - `01AEND` → `'E'`, adds `WS-FULL-ENDOW-LEN` (124) to required length
   - `01AHOU` → `'H'`, adds `WS-FULL-HOUSE-LEN` (130)
   - `01AMOT` → `'M'`, adds `WS-FULL-MOTOR-LEN` (137)
   - `01ACOM` → `'C'`, adds `WS-FULL-COMM-LEN` (1174)
2. **`INSERT INTO POLICY`** — `POLICYNUMBER` assigned by DB2 IDENTITY, `LASTCHANGED` set to `CURRENT TIMESTAMP`
3. **Retrieves assigned policy number** via `IDENTITY_VAL_LOCAL()` → `CA-POLICY-NUM` (returned to caller)
4. **`INSERT INTO` type-specific table** (ENDOWMENT/HOUSE/MOTOR/COMMERCIAL)
   - On failure: `ABEND 'LGSQ'` → forces CICS to **backout the POLICY INSERT** (unit of work)
5. **`EXEC CICS LINK Program(LGAPVS01)`** — write VSAM secondary record

**This implements the two-phase commit pattern**: DB2 first, VSAM only on DB2 success.

**`LGAPVS01`** writes a **64-byte summary record** to `KSDSPOLY` VSAM KSDS with key: `[policy type 1 byte] + [customer num 10 bytes] + [policy num 10 bytes]`.

---

### Error Path (Any Tier)

Any error in any program calls `LGSTSQ`, which writes a diagnostic message to:
- **`CSMT` TDQ** — CICS system operations log
- **`GENAERRS` TSQ** — GenApp developer error store (browsable)

---

## 📊 Side-by-Side Comparison: Before vs. After Documentation

| Question | Without Docs (Lab 2 Ex 1) | With Docs (Now) |
|---|---|---|
| Which programs are involved? | "Probably lgapol01, lgapdb01, lgapvs01" (guessed) | Full 3-tier chain confirmed with exact CICS LINK calls |
| What data flows between them? | "COMMAREA, likely lgcmarea.cpy" | Specific: CA-REQUEST-ID routing, CA-RETURN-CODE handshake, WS-FULL-*-LEN from lgpolicy.cpy |
| Where does validation happen? | "Probably in the business logic layer" | Two exact points: EIBCALEN=0 → ABEND LGCA; EIBCALEN < required → RC 98 |
| DB2 write order? | Not answered | POLICY first, then type-specific — ABEND LGSQ if type table fails |
| Policy number assignment? | Not mentioned | DB2 IDENTITY_VAL_LOCAL() → CA-POLICY-NUM returned to caller |
| VSAM write? | "lgapvs01 for secondary store" | Called from LGAPDB01 after DB2 success; writes 64-byte summary; key = type+custnum+polnum |
| Error handling? | Not mentioned | LGSTSQ → GENAERRS TSQ + CSMT TDQ from any tier |
| Confidence | Low — must read 6+ programs | High — grounded in generated documentation |

---

## 🎓 What the Documentation Enabled

1. **Cross-program reasoning** — Bob can trace the full flow across 3 tiers without reading each program
2. **Business-level answers** — "two-phase commit pattern", "unit of work rollback via ABEND LGSQ" are now answerable
3. **Precise field references** — `CA-RETURN-CODE`, `WS-CA-HEADER-LEN`, `IDENTITY_VAL_LOCAL()` — named correctly
4. **Architecture insight** — the "business logic is field-agnostic" principle only becomes visible with cross-program documentation

**The documentation value chain in action:**
```
Source code → Program docs (14 files) → Application HTML (16 pages) → Precise answers
```

LGAPOL01 — Add Policy

Business Logic Layer · CICS GenApp

🏠 Home🏗 Architecture Add PolicyInquire Policy Update PolicyDelete Policy 📋 Copybooks
← Back to Index Business Logic

Overview

LGAPOL01 is the business logic layer for adding a new insurance policy. It validates COMMAREA presence and minimum length, then delegates the actual DB2 INSERT to LGAPDB01 via EXEC CICS LINK. This program is intentionally field-agnostic — it does not interpret individual policy fields. All field-level logic lives in the data layer.

Policy types supported: Endowment (E), House (H), Motor (M), Commercial (C).

Inputs

SourceFieldDescription
COMMAREACA-REQUEST-ID01AEND=Endowment, 01AHOU=House, 01AMOT=Motor, 01ACOM=Commercial
COMMAREACA-CUSTOMER-NUM10-digit customer identifier
COMMAREACA-POLICY-COMMONIssue date, expiry date, broker ID, payment
COMMAREAPolicy-specific fieldsCA-ENDOWMENT / CA-HOUSE / CA-MOTOR / CA-COMMERCIAL (REDEFINES)
EIBEIBCALENMust be ≥ 28 bytes (WS-CA-HEADER-LEN)

Processing Logic

  1. Initialize WS-HEADER — capture transaction ID, terminal ID, task number
  2. Check EIBCALEN = 0 → write error via LGSTSQ, then ABEND 'LGCA' (no recovery)
  3. Initialize return code: CA-RETURN-CODE = '00'
  4. Check EIBCALEN < WS-CA-HEADER-LEN (28) → CA-RETURN-CODE = '98', CICS RETURN
  5. EXEC CICS LINK Program(LGAPDB01) Commarea(DFHCOMMAREA) LENGTH(32500)
  6. EXEC CICS RETURN — return to caller with result in CA-RETURN-CODE and CA-POLICY-NUM

Programs Called

ProgramCall TypePurpose
LGAPDB01EXEC CICS LINKDB2 INSERT — POLICY + type-specific table + VSAM write via LGAPVS01
LGSTSQEXEC CICS LINKError message writer — GENAERRS TSQ + CSMT TDQ

Copybooks Used

CopybookPurpose
lgcmarea.cpyCOMMAREA structure — all inter-program fields

Error Handling

ConditionReturn CodeAction
EIBCALEN = 0N/AWrite error → ABEND 'LGCA' — no recovery
EIBCALEN < 28'98'CICS RETURN immediately
DB2 / VSAM errorsSet by LGAPDB01Propagated back through COMMAREA

Business Rules

  • Minimum COMMAREA is 28 bytes (header only) — type-specific length validated in LGAPDB01
  • LGAPOL01 is completely field-agnostic — adding a new policy field never requires changing this program
  • The policy number (CA-POLICY-NUM) is DB2 IDENTITY-assigned and returned in COMMAREA
  • Both DB2 and VSAM writes are triggered from within LGAPDB01 (two-phase: DB2 first, VSAM on success)

LGAPDB01 — Add Policy DB2

DB2 Data Management Layer · CICS GenApp

🏠 Home🏗 Architecture Add PolicyInquire Policy Update PolicyDelete Policy 📋 Copybooks
← Back to Index DB2 Data Layer

Overview

Called via EXEC CICS LINK from LGAPOL01, LGAPDB01 routes by CA-REQUEST-ID, validates COMMAREA length per policy type, inserts into the POLICY table and the type-specific table, then calls LGAPVS01 for the VSAM secondary write.

Returns the DB2-assigned policy number in CA-POLICY-NUM and the timestamp in CA-LASTCHANGED.

COMMAREA Length Requirements

Request IDPolicy TypeExtra Length ConstantValue
01AENDEndowmentWS-FULL-ENDOW-LEN124 bytes
01AHOUHouseWS-FULL-HOUSE-LEN130 bytes
01AMOTMotorWS-FULL-MOTOR-LEN137 bytes
01ACOMCommercialWS-FULL-COMM-LEN1174 bytes

Processing Logic

  1. Initialize WS-HEADER, DB2 host variables
  2. Check EIBCALEN = 0 → ABEND 'LGCA'
  3. EVALUATE CA-REQUEST-ID — set DB2-POLICYTYPE and add type-specific length to required CA length; unknown type → RC '99'
  4. Check EIBCALEN < required length → RC '98', RETURN
  5. PERFORM INSERT-POLICY — INSERT INTO POLICY with IDENTITY for POLICYNUMBER and CURRENT TIMESTAMP for LASTCHANGED
  6. Retrieve assigned policy number: IDENTITY_VAL_LOCAL() → CA-POLICY-NUM
  7. Retrieve LASTCHANGED timestamp via SELECT
  8. EVALUATE CA-REQUEST-ID → PERFORM INSERT-ENDOW / INSERT-HOUSE / INSERT-MOTOR / INSERT-COMMERCIAL
  9. EXEC CICS LINK Program(LGAPVS01) — VSAM secondary write
  10. EXEC CICS RETURN
💡 Two-Phase Commit: On type-specific INSERT failure, EXEC CICS ABEND ABCODE('LGSQ') forces CICS to backout the POLICY INSERT. This ensures both writes succeed or both are rolled back.

Programs Called

ProgramCall TypePurpose

LGSTSQEXEC CICS LINKError message writer — GENAERRS + CSMT

SQL Includes / Copybooks

IncludePurpose

LGCMAREACOMMAREA structure
SQLCADB2 SQLCODE / SQLSTATE

Error Handling

SQLCODEReturn CodeMeaning
0'00'Success
-530'70'FK violation — customer not found
Other (POLICY)'90'DB2 error — log to LGSTSQ, RETURN
Non-zero (type table)'90'ABEND 'LGSQ' — forces backout of POLICY INSERT

Business Rules

  • Policy number is DB2-assigned via IDENTITY column — never passed in by caller
  • ABEND 'LGSQ' on type INSERT failure ensures unit-of-work integrity
  • Commercial policies have the largest COMMAREA requirement (1174 bytes)
  • VSAM write (LGAPVS01) is always called after DB2 success — no conditional check

Called from LGIPOL01, LGIPDB01 handles 7 inquiry variants by routing on CA-REQUEST-ID. It performs DB2 SELECTs on joins of the POLICY table with type-specific tables, and populates the COMMAREA with retrieved data.

01IHOUInquire House by policy#Single SELECT — POLICY JOIN HOUSE

SQLCODEReturn CodeMeaning
0'00'Row found — data populated in COMMAREA
100'01'No rows found

LGAPVS01 — Add Policy VSAM

VSAM Data Management Layer · CICS GenApp

🏠 Home🏗 Architecture Add PolicyInquire Policy Update PolicyDelete Policy 📋 Copybooks
← Back to Index VSAM Data Layer

Overview

Called via EXEC CICS LINK from LGAPDB01, LGAPVS01 writes a 64-byte summary record to the KSDSPOLY VSAM KSDS file. This is the second phase of the two-phase commit: DB2 (primary) → VSAM (secondary, on DB2 success only).

VSAM Record Layout (64 bytes)

FieldSizeDescription
WF-Request-ID1 bytePolicy type: C, E, H, or M (from CA-REQUEST-ID 4th char)
WF-Customer-Num10 bytesCustomer number
WF-Policy-Num10 bytesPolicy number
WF-Policy-Data43 bytesType-specific summary (REDEFINES per type)

Type-Specific Summary Data

TypeFields Stored in WF-Policy-Data
C (Commercial)Postcode (8), Status (4), Customer (31)
E (Endowment)WITH-PROFITS (1), EQUITIES (1), MANAGED-FUND (1), FUND-NAME (10), LIFE-ASSURED (30)
H (House)PROPERTY-TYPE (15), BEDROOMS (3), VALUE (8), POSTCODE (8), HOUSE-NAME (9)
M (Motor)MAKE (15), MODEL (15), VALUE (6), REGNUMBER (7)

Processing Logic

  1. Extract policy type from CA-REQUEST-ID(4:1) → WF-Request-ID
  2. Copy CA-POLICY-NUM and CA-CUSTOMER-NUM to key fields
  3. EVALUATE WF-Request-ID — populate type-specific WF-Policy-Data from COMMAREA
  4. EXEC CICS WRITE FILE('KSDSPOLY') FROM(WF-Policy-Info) LENGTH(64) RIDFLD(WF-Policy-Key) KEYLENGTH(21)
  5. If RESP ≠ DFHRESP(NORMAL) → RC '80', log RESP + RESP2 to LGSTSQ, RETURN

Programs Called

ProgramCall TypePurpose
LGSTSQEXEC CICS LINKError writer (VSAM write failure only)

Business Rules

  • VSAM stores only a summary — not the full DB2 record
  • Called only after successful DB2 INSERT (two-phase pattern)
  • VSAM key includes policy type as first byte — allows type-aware lookups
  • WHEN OTHER → SPACES in WF-Policy-Data — prevents garbage data on unknown type
  • DB2 is the authoritative store; VSAM is secondary/summary

LGSTSQ — Error/Message Writer

Utility Program · CICS GenApp

🏠 Home🏗 Architecture Add PolicyInquire Policy Update PolicyDelete Policy 📋 Copybooks
← Back to Index Utility

Overview

LGSTSQ is GenApp's centralized error logging utility. It writes diagnostic messages to two destinations simultaneously — the CICS system log and a GenApp-specific developer queue. It is called by every GenApp program in its WRITE-ERROR-MESSAGE paragraph.

Can be invoked via CICS LINK (from a program) or run as a standalone CICS transaction (from 3270 terminal).

📢 Called by: LGAPOL01, LGIPOL01, LGUPOL01, LGDPOL01, LGAPDB01, LGIPDB01, LGUPDB01, LGDPDB01, LGAPVS01, LGIPVS01, LGUPVS01, LGDPVS01 — every program in GenApp

Output Queues

QueueTypeNameAudience
System logTDQ (Transient Data)CSMTCICS operations team — persistent
GenApp storeTSQ (Temporary Storage)GENAERRS (default) or GENAxxxxDevelopers — browsable

Processing Logic

  1. EXEC CICS ASSIGN SYSID — get system ID for message prefix
  2. EXEC CICS ASSIGN INVOKINGPROG — determine invocation mode
  3. If INVOKINGPROG non-blank → LINK mode: use COMMA-DATA (90 bytes of COMMAREA) as message
  4. Else → Transaction mode: EXEC CICS RECEIVE from terminal
  5. Check message prefix Q=xxxx → override TSQ name to GENAxxxx
  6. EXEC CICS WRITEQ TD QUEUE('CSMT') — write to system TDQ
  7. EXEC CICS WRITEQ TS QUEUE(STSQ-NAME) NOSUSPEND — write to GenApp TSQ
  8. If terminal mode → EXEC CICS SEND TEXT ... FREEKB — clear screen
  9. EXEC CICS RETURN

Business Rules

  • NOSUSPEND on TSQ write — if storage exhausted, write is silently dropped (never causes the calling program to wait)
  • Two writes per call — TDQ for ops (CSMT), TSQ for developers (GENAERRS)
  • Queue override (Q=xxxx prefix) routes messages to a specific sub-queue for targeted debugging
  • Message format: SYSID (4) + space (1) + message text (90) = 95 bytes max
  • This is the single point of error persistence for all of GenApp — no program writes errors directly to queues

LGIPOL01 — Inquire Policy

Business Logic Layer · CICS GenApp

🏠 Home🏗 Architecture Add PolicyInquire Policy Update PolicyDelete Policy 📋 Copybooks
← Back to Index Business Logic

Overview

LGIPOL01 is the business logic layer for insurance policy inquiry. It validates COMMAREA presence, then delegates all data retrieval to LGIPDB01 via EXEC CICS LINK. Like all business logic programs, it is field-agnostic — routing by CA-REQUEST-ID happens entirely in LGIPDB01.

Supports 7 inquiry variants: by policy number (E/H/M/C), by customer (all commercial), by ZIP code.

Inputs

SourceFieldDescription
COMMAREACA-REQUEST-ID01IEND, 01IHOU, 01IMOT, 01ICOM, 02ICOM, 03ICOM, 05ICOM
COMMAREACA-CUSTOMER-NUM10-digit customer identifier
COMMAREACA-POLICY-NUMPolicy number to retrieve
EIBEIBCALENMust be > 0

Processing Logic

  1. Initialize WS-HEADER
  2. Check EIBCALEN = 0 → write error, ABEND 'LGCA'
  3. Initialize CA-RETURN-CODE = '00'; save EIBCALEN
  4. EXEC CICS LINK Program(LGIPDB01) Commarea(DFHCOMMAREA) LENGTH(32500)
  5. EXEC CICS RETURN

Programs Called

ProgramCall TypePurpose
LGIPDB01EXEC CICS LINKDB2 SELECT — routes by CA-REQUEST-ID, populates COMMAREA with policy data
LGSTSQEXEC CICS LINKError message writer

Copybooks Used

CopybookPurpose
lgcmarea.cpyCOMMAREA structure
lgpolicy.cpyDB2 record length definitions

Error Handling

ConditionAction
EIBCALEN = 0ABEND 'LGCA' — no recovery
All data errorsHandled in LGIPDB01 — RC 01 (not found), 90 (DB2 error), 98 (COMMAREA short)

Business Rules

  • No COMMAREA = hard ABEND — non-recoverable
  • Policy type routing (7 variants) handled entirely in LGIPDB01
  • LGIPOL01 never reads or writes any policy field directly

LGAPOL01 — Add Policy

Business Logic Layer · CICS GenApp

🏠 Home🏗 Architecture Add PolicyInquire Policy Update PolicyDelete Policy 📋 Copybooks
← Back to Index Business Logic

Overview

LGAPOL01 is the business logic layer for adding a new insurance policy. It validates COMMAREA presence and minimum length, then delegates the actual DB2 INSERT to LGAPDB01 via EXEC CICS LINK. This program is intentionally field-agnostic — it does not interpret individual policy fields. All field-level logic lives in the data layer.

Policy types supported: Endowment (E), House (H), Motor (M), Commercial (C).

Inputs

SourceFieldDescription
COMMAREACA-REQUEST-ID01AEND=Endowment, 01AHOU=House, 01AMOT=Motor, 01ACOM=Commercial
COMMAREACA-CUSTOMER-NUM10-digit customer identifier
COMMAREACA-POLICY-COMMONIssue date, expiry date, broker ID, payment
COMMAREAPolicy-specific fieldsCA-ENDOWMENT / CA-HOUSE / CA-MOTOR / CA-COMMERCIAL (REDEFINES)
EIBEIBCALENMust be ≥ 28 bytes (WS-CA-HEADER-LEN)

Processing Logic

  1. Initialize WS-HEADER — capture transaction ID, terminal ID, task number
  2. Check EIBCALEN = 0 → write error via LGSTSQ, then ABEND 'LGCA' (no recovery)
  3. Initialize return code: CA-RETURN-CODE = '00'
  4. Check EIBCALEN < WS-CA-HEADER-LEN (28) → CA-RETURN-CODE = '98', CICS RETURN
  5. EXEC CICS LINK Program(LGAPDB01) Commarea(DFHCOMMAREA) LENGTH(32500)
  6. EXEC CICS RETURN — return to caller with result in CA-RETURN-CODE and CA-POLICY-NUM

Programs Called

ProgramCall TypePurpose
LGAPDB01EXEC CICS LINKDB2 INSERT — POLICY + type-specific table + VSAM write via LGAPVS01
LGSTSQEXEC CICS LINKError message writer — GENAERRS TSQ + CSMT TDQ

Copybooks Used

CopybookPurpose
lgcmarea.cpyCOMMAREA structure — all inter-program fields

Error Handling

ConditionReturn CodeAction
EIBCALEN = 0N/AWrite error → ABEND 'LGCA' — no recovery
EIBCALEN < 28'98'CICS RETURN immediately
DB2 / VSAM errorsSet by LGAPDB01Propagated back through COMMAREA

Business Rules

  • Minimum COMMAREA is 28 bytes (header only) — type-specific length validated in LGAPDB01
  • LGAPOL01 is completely field-agnostic — adding a new policy field never requires changing this program
  • The policy number (CA-POLICY-NUM) is DB2 IDENTITY-assigned and returned in COMMAREA
  • Both DB2 and VSAM writes are triggered from within LGAPDB01 (two-phase: DB2 first, VSAM on success)

LGUPOL01 — Update Policy

Business Logic Layer · CICS GenApp

🏠 Home🏗 Architecture Add PolicyInquire Policy Update PolicyDelete Policy 📋 Copybooks
← Back to Index Business Logic

Overview

LGUPOL01 is the business logic layer for updating an insurance policy. Unlike LGAPOL01, it performs per-type COMMAREA length validation before delegating to LGUPDB01.

Supported: Endowment, House, Motor. Commercial update is not currently supported — see Known Gap below.

COMMAREA Length Requirements

Policy TypeRequest IDMinimum COMMAREA
Endowment01UEND28 (header) + 124 (endow) = 152 bytes
House01UHOU28 (header) + 130 (house) = 158 bytes
Motor01UMOT28 (header) + 137 (motor) = 165 bytes

Processing Logic

  1. Initialize WS-HEADER
  2. Check EIBCALEN = 0 → ABEND 'LGCA'
  3. Initialize CA-RETURN-CODE = '00'
  4. EVALUATE CA-REQUEST-ID — check minimum COMMAREA per type; unknown → RC '99'; too short → RC '98', RETURN
  5. PERFORM UPDATE-POLICY-DB2-INFO → EXEC CICS LINK Program(LGUPDB01)
  6. EXEC CICS RETURN

Programs Called

ProgramCall TypePurpose
LGUPDB01EXEC CICS LINKDB2 UPDATE — POLICY table + type-specific table
LGSTSQEXEC CICS LINKError message writer

Copybooks Used

CopybookPurpose
lgcmarea.cpyCOMMAREA structure

Error Handling

ConditionReturn Code
No COMMAREAABEND 'LGCA'
Unknown request ID'99'
COMMAREA too short'98'
DB2 UPDATE failureSet in LGUPDB01
⚠️ Known Gap: Commercial policy update (01UCOM) is not handled — falls to WHEN OTHER → RC '99'. To add support, add a WHEN '01UCOM' clause with WS-FULL-COMM-LEN check and update LGUPDB01.

LGAPDB01 — Add Policy DB2

DB2 Data Management Layer · CICS GenApp

🏠 Home🏗 Architecture Add PolicyInquire Policy Update PolicyDelete Policy 📋 Copybooks
← Back to Index DB2 Data Layer

Overview

Called via EXEC CICS LINK from LGAPOL01, LGAPDB01 routes by CA-REQUEST-ID, validates COMMAREA length per policy type, inserts into the POLICY table and the type-specific table, then calls LGAPVS01 for the VSAM secondary write.

Returns the DB2-assigned policy number in CA-POLICY-NUM and the timestamp in CA-LASTCHANGED.

COMMAREA Length Requirements

Request IDPolicy TypeExtra Length ConstantValue
01AENDEndowmentWS-FULL-ENDOW-LEN124 bytes
01AHOUHouseWS-FULL-HOUSE-LEN130 bytes
01AMOTMotorWS-FULL-MOTOR-LEN137 bytes
01ACOMCommercialWS-FULL-COMM-LEN1174 bytes

Processing Logic

  1. Initialize WS-HEADER, DB2 host variables
  2. Check EIBCALEN = 0 → ABEND 'LGCA'
  3. EVALUATE CA-REQUEST-ID — set DB2-POLICYTYPE and add type-specific length to required CA length; unknown type → RC '99'
  4. Check EIBCALEN < required length → RC '98', RETURN
  5. PERFORM INSERT-POLICY — INSERT INTO POLICY with IDENTITY for POLICYNUMBER and CURRENT TIMESTAMP for LASTCHANGED
  6. Retrieve assigned policy number: IDENTITY_VAL_LOCAL() → CA-POLICY-NUM
  7. Retrieve LASTCHANGED timestamp via SELECT
  8. EVALUATE CA-REQUEST-ID → PERFORM INSERT-ENDOW / INSERT-HOUSE / INSERT-MOTOR / INSERT-COMMERCIAL
  9. EXEC CICS LINK Program(LGAPVS01) — VSAM secondary write
  10. EXEC CICS RETURN
💡 Two-Phase Commit: On type-specific INSERT failure, EXEC CICS ABEND ABCODE('LGSQ') forces CICS to backout the POLICY INSERT. This ensures both writes succeed or both are rolled back.

Programs Called

ProgramCall TypePurpose
LGAPVS01EXEC CICS LINKWrite 64-byte policy summary to KSDSPOLY VSAM
LGSTSQEXEC CICS LINKError message writer — GENAERRS + CSMT

SQL Includes / Copybooks

IncludePurpose
LGPOLICYDB2 record structures and length constants
LGCMAREACOMMAREA structure
SQLCADB2 SQLCODE / SQLSTATE

Error Handling

SQLCODEReturn CodeMeaning
0'00'Success
-530'70'FK violation — customer not found
Other (POLICY)'90'DB2 error — log to LGSTSQ, RETURN
Non-zero (type table)'90'ABEND 'LGSQ' — forces backout of POLICY INSERT

Business Rules

  • Policy number is DB2-assigned via IDENTITY column — never passed in by caller
  • ABEND 'LGSQ' on type INSERT failure ensures unit-of-work integrity
  • Commercial policies have the largest COMMAREA requirement (1174 bytes)
  • VSAM write (LGAPVS01) is always called after DB2 success — no conditional check
Generated by IBM Bob Premium Package for Z · GenApp Application Knowledge Base · 2025

LGIPDB01 — Inquire Policy DB2

DB2 Data Management Layer · CICS GenApp

🏠 Home🏗 Architecture Add PolicyInquire Policy Update PolicyDelete Policy 📋 Copybooks
← Back to Index DB2 Data Layer

Overview

Called from LGIPOL01, LGIPDB01 handles 7 inquiry variants by routing on CA-REQUEST-ID. It performs DB2 SELECTs on joins of the POLICY table with type-specific tables, and populates the COMMAREA with retrieved data.

Inquiry Variants

Request IDOperationDB2 Approach
01IENDInquire Endowment by policy#Single SELECT — POLICY JOIN ENDOWMENT
01IHOUInquire House by policy#Single SELECT — POLICY JOIN HOUSE
01IMOTInquire Motor by policy#Single SELECT — POLICY JOIN MOTOR
01ICOMInquire Commercial by customer+policySingle SELECT — POLICY JOIN COMMERCIAL
02ICOMInquire Commercial by policy# onlySingle SELECT — POLICY JOIN COMMERCIAL
03ICOMAll Commercial for a customerCursor Cust_Cursor — up to 20 rows
05ICOMCommercial by ZIP/postcodeCursor Zip_Cursor — all matching rows

Programs Called

ProgramCall TypePurpose
LGSTSQEXEC CICS LINKError message writer

Error Handling

SQLCODEReturn CodeMeaning
0'00'Row found — data populated in COMMAREA
100'01'No rows found
Other'90'DB2 error — logged to LGSTSQ
Cursor open fail'89'Cursor open error
Cursor close fail'88'Cursor close error

Business Rules

  • NULL handling: BROKERID, BROKERSREF, PAYMENT use indicator variables — NULLs are not moved
  • Endowment VARCHAR: PADDINGDATA length checked via indicator; conditional COMMAREA population
  • FINAL marker: written to trailing FILLER after policy data — signals end-of-data to caller
  • Commercial cursor cap: 03ICOM limited to 20 records (ICOM-Record-Count > 20 → SQLCODE=17)
  • COMMAREA size check: if retrieved data exceeds COMMAREA received → RC '98'

LGAPVS01 — Add Policy VSAM

VSAM Data Management Layer · CICS GenApp

🏠 Home🏗 Architecture Add PolicyInquire Policy Update PolicyDelete Policy 📋 Copybooks
← Back to Index VSAM Data Layer

Overview

Called via EXEC CICS LINK from LGAPDB01, LGAPVS01 writes a 64-byte summary record to the KSDSPOLY VSAM KSDS file. This is the second phase of the two-phase commit: DB2 (primary) → VSAM (secondary, on DB2 success only).

VSAM Record Layout (64 bytes)

FieldSizeDescription
WF-Request-ID1 bytePolicy type: C, E, H, or M (from CA-REQUEST-ID 4th char)
WF-Customer-Num10 bytesCustomer number
WF-Policy-Num10 bytesPolicy number
WF-Policy-Data43 bytesType-specific summary (REDEFINES per type)

Type-Specific Summary Data

TypeFields Stored in WF-Policy-Data
C (Commercial)Postcode (8), Status (4), Customer (31)
E (Endowment)WITH-PROFITS (1), EQUITIES (1), MANAGED-FUND (1), FUND-NAME (10), LIFE-ASSURED (30)
H (House)PROPERTY-TYPE (15), BEDROOMS (3), VALUE (8), POSTCODE (8), HOUSE-NAME (9)
M (Motor)MAKE (15), MODEL (15), VALUE (6), REGNUMBER (7)

Processing Logic

  1. Extract policy type from CA-REQUEST-ID(4:1) → WF-Request-ID
  2. Copy CA-POLICY-NUM and CA-CUSTOMER-NUM to key fields
  3. EVALUATE WF-Request-ID — populate type-specific WF-Policy-Data from COMMAREA
  4. EXEC CICS WRITE FILE('KSDSPOLY') FROM(WF-Policy-Info) LENGTH(64) RIDFLD(WF-Policy-Key) KEYLENGTH(21)
  5. If RESP ≠ DFHRESP(NORMAL) → RC '80', log RESP + RESP2 to LGSTSQ, RETURN

Programs Called

ProgramCall TypePurpose
LGSTSQEXEC CICS LINKError writer (VSAM write failure only)

Business Rules

  • VSAM stores only a summary — not the full DB2 record
  • Called only after successful DB2 INSERT (two-phase pattern)
  • VSAM key includes policy type as first byte — allows type-aware lookups
  • WHEN OTHER → SPACES in WF-Policy-Data — prevents garbage data on unknown type
  • DB2 is the authoritative store; VSAM is secondary/summary

LGDPOL01 — Delete Policy

Business Logic Layer · CICS GenApp

🏠 Home🏗 Architecture Add PolicyInquire Policy Update PolicyDelete Policy 📋 Copybooks
← Back to Index Business Logic

Overview

LGDPOL01 is the business logic layer for deleting an insurance policy. It validates the request ID, upper-cases it (safe for 3270 input), and delegates to LGDPDB01 via EXEC CICS LINK.

All four policy types are supported for delete: Endowment, House, Motor, Commercial.

Inputs

SourceFieldDescription
COMMAREACA-REQUEST-ID01DEND, 01DMOT, 01DHOU, 01DCOM
COMMAREACA-CUSTOMER-NUMCustomer number
COMMAREACA-POLICY-NUMPolicy number to delete
EIBEIBCALENMust be ≥ 28 bytes

Processing Logic

  1. Initialize WS-HEADER
  2. Check EIBCALEN = 0 → write error, ABEND 'LGCA'
  3. Initialize CA-RETURN-CODE = '00'
  4. Check EIBCALEN < 28 → RC '98', RETURN
  5. Upper-case CA-REQUEST-ID via FUNCTION UPPER-CASE
  6. Validate: must be 01DEND, 01DMOT, 01DHOU, or 01DCOM; else RC '99'
  7. PERFORM DELETE-POLICY-DB2-INFO → EXEC CICS LINK Program(LGDPDB01)
  8. If CA-RETURN-CODE > 0 after delete → RETURN
  9. EXEC CICS RETURN

Programs Called

ProgramCall TypePurpose
LGDPDB01EXEC CICS LINKDB2 DELETE — removes from POLICY + type table
LGSTSQEXEC CICS LINKError message writer

Copybooks Used

CopybookPurpose
lgcmarea.cpyCOMMAREA structure

Error Handling

ConditionReturn Code
No COMMAREAABEND 'LGCA'
COMMAREA < 28 bytes'98'
Unknown request ID'99'
DB2 DELETE failureSet in LGDPDB01

Business Rules

  • Delete requires only the 28-byte header — no policy-specific fields needed
  • CA-REQUEST-ID is upper-cased before validation — safe for 3270 mixed-case input
  • All four policy types (E, H, M, C) supported for deletion
  • Existence check handled by LGDPDB01 (SQLCODE 100 = not found)

LGSTSQ — Error/Message Writer

Utility Program · CICS GenApp

🏠 Home🏗 Architecture Add PolicyInquire Policy Update PolicyDelete Policy 📋 Copybooks
← Back to Index Utility

Overview

LGSTSQ is GenApp's centralized error logging utility. It writes diagnostic messages to two destinations simultaneously — the CICS system log and a GenApp-specific developer queue. It is called by every GenApp program in its WRITE-ERROR-MESSAGE paragraph.

Can be invoked via CICS LINK (from a program) or run as a standalone CICS transaction (from 3270 terminal).

📢 Called by: LGAPOL01, LGIPOL01, LGUPOL01, LGDPOL01, LGAPDB01, LGIPDB01, LGUPDB01, LGDPDB01, LGAPVS01, LGIPVS01, LGUPVS01, LGDPVS01 — every program in GenApp

Output Queues

QueueTypeNameAudience
System logTDQ (Transient Data)CSMTCICS operations team — persistent
GenApp storeTSQ (Temporary Storage)GENAERRS (default) or GENAxxxxDevelopers — browsable

Processing Logic

  1. EXEC CICS ASSIGN SYSID — get system ID for message prefix
  2. EXEC CICS ASSIGN INVOKINGPROG — determine invocation mode
  3. If INVOKINGPROG non-blank → LINK mode: use COMMA-DATA (90 bytes of COMMAREA) as message
  4. Else → Transaction mode: EXEC CICS RECEIVE from terminal
  5. Check message prefix Q=xxxx → override TSQ name to GENAxxxx
  6. EXEC CICS WRITEQ TD QUEUE('CSMT') — write to system TDQ
  7. EXEC CICS WRITEQ TS QUEUE(STSQ-NAME) NOSUSPEND — write to GenApp TSQ
  8. If terminal mode → EXEC CICS SEND TEXT ... FREEKB — clear screen
  9. EXEC CICS RETURN

Business Rules

  • NOSUSPEND on TSQ write — if storage exhausted, write is silently dropped (never causes the calling program to wait)
  • Two writes per call — TDQ for ops (CSMT), TSQ for developers (GENAERRS)
  • Queue override (Q=xxxx prefix) routes messages to a specific sub-queue for targeted debugging
  • Message format: SYSID (4) + space (1) + message text (90) = 95 bytes max
  • This is the single point of error persistence for all of GenApp — no program writes errors directly to queues

LGAPOL01

Business Logic Layer — Add Policy

🏠 Home 🏗 Architecture Add Policy Inquire Policy Update Policy Delete Policy 📋 Copybooks
← Back to Index Business Logic

Overview

LGAPOL01 is the business logic layer for adding a new insurance policy in GenApp. It validates the presence and minimum length of the COMMAREA, then delegates the actual DB2 INSERT to LGAPDB01 via EXEC CICS LINK. This program is deliberately field-agnostic — it has no knowledge of individual policy fields.

Supported policy types: Endowment (E), House (H), Motor (M), Commercial (C).

Inputs

SourceFieldDescription
COMMAREACA-REQUEST-IDOperation code: 01AEND, 01AHOU, 01AMOT, 01ACOM
COMMAREACA-CUSTOMER-NUM10-digit customer identifier
COMMAREACA-POLICY-COMMONIssue date, expiry date, broker ID, payment
COMMAREAPolicy-specific fieldsCA-ENDOWMENT / CA-HOUSE / CA-MOTOR / CA-COMMERCIAL (REDEFINES)
EIBEIBCALENCICS commarea length — must be > 0 and ≥ 28

Processing Logic

  1. Initialize WS-HEADER — captures EIBTRNID, EIBTRMID, EIBTASKN
  2. If EIBCALEN = 0 → write error via LGSTSQ → EXEC CICS ABEND ABCODE('LGCA')
  3. Set CA-RETURN-CODE = '00'
  4. If EIBCALEN < WS-CA-HEADER-LEN (28) → CA-RETURN-CODE = '98' → CICS RETURN
  5. EXEC CICS LINK Program(LGAPDB01) Commarea(DFHCOMMAREA) LENGTH(32500)
  6. EXEC CICS RETURN

Programs Called

ProgramCall TypePurpose
LGAPDB01EXEC CICS LINKDB2 INSERT — POLICY table + type-specific table; also calls LGAPVS01
LGSTSQEXEC CICS LINKError message writer — GENAERRS TSQ + CSMT TDQ

Copybooks Used

CopybookPurpose
lgcmarea.cpyCOMMAREA structure — all inter-program fields

Error Handling

ConditionReturn CodeAction
EIBCALEN = 0N/AABEND 'LGCA' — no recovery
EIBCALEN < 28'98'CICS RETURN immediately
DB2 errorsSet in LGAPDB01Handled entirely within LGAPDB01

Business Rules

  • Minimum COMMAREA is 28 bytes (header only) — additional length checked in LGAPDB01
  • This program is field-agnostic — adding a new policy field never requires changes here
  • The policy number is assigned by DB2 IDENTITY and returned in CA-POLICY-NUM
  • Both DB2 and VSAM writes are triggered within LGAPDB01 (two-phase commit pattern)
